projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

The stable presence of 12–14 devices over the last four hours paired with zero camera motion detection indicates the household is likely home and settled in blind spots or engaged in low-activity routines; this warrants a quick verification that cameras are functioning normally and that everyone is safe, as prolonged inactivity despite high device count is atypical for a Friday afternoon.

The stable presence count of 12 devices since 13:31, combined with zero camera activity, confirms a quiet, undisturbed afternoon with no unusual movement or visitors, consistent with normal Friday routines.

The connected device count has steadily declined from 14 to 12 over the last three hours, with a brief reconnect at 13:26, suggesting someone is gradually leaving the house or devices are being powered down and moved out of Wi-Fi range. Given the Friday afternoon timing, this likely indicates the family is packing up for a weekend outing or activity.

The stable presence of 13-14 mobile devices from 05:14 to 08:52 confirms the entire household is still at home, which is later than the typical Friday morning departure window and may indicate a late start or remote work day.

The consistent 13–15 device count with frequent oscillations at 3:52 AM, paired with zero camera activity, strongly indicates background IoT device polling rather than human presence. The oscillations align with typical network sleep/wake cycles, confirming this is benign household electronics activity.

The sustained high device count (14–16) with frequent oscillations, combined with zero camera activity at this late Friday hour, strongly indicates Miller and Penelope are awake in their rooms actively using multiple personal devices, while the adults are likely asleep. This cross-signal pattern confirms a normal weekend wind-down rather than a network fault, though the constant polling may be draining device batteries.

The rapid oscillation between 13 and 14 connected devices over the past 75 minutes, paired with zero camera activity at night, indicates Wi-Fi roaming instability or IoT devices cycling connection states rather than actual household movement. This pattern suggests a network health issue that could cause false presence alerts, warranting a router or access point check.

The stable 14-16 device count confirms full occupancy, while the prolonged zero camera motion strongly suggests the family is gathered in a single area or the cameras are in low-sensitivity mode; this is a benign evening pattern but worth verifying camera configuration if it persists.

The sustained 14-16 device count confirms occupancy, but the complete lack of camera motion during typical evening hours strongly indicates a camera blind spot, system failure, or disabled feeds, leaving the home effectively blind to activity and potential safety or security events.
